questions.prompt: RouteIQ enforces its delivery-proof contract in a client store because it has no server. If the same contract moved into a server route handler, which three things would change, which checks must live on the server and why, what is still worth keeping on the client, and what can no client validator ever establish?

keyPoints.text: On a server, rejection replaces silent dropping and the response gets a 400 shape that tells the caller what was refused.
keyPoints.quote: rejection replaces silent dropping, the response has a 400 shape

keyPoints.text: Ownership is checked from the session instead of trusted from the client: driverId comes from the session, never the body.
keyPoints.quote: `driverId` comes from the session, never the body

keyPoints.text: The server must also check that the stop is still pending before recording an outcome.
keyPoints.quote: the `pending` state check

keyPoints.text: The proof and the delivery event are written in one transaction.
keyPoints.quote: the proof and the event in one transaction

keyPoints.text: The size limit must be server-side because a client can bypass any store.
keyPoints.quote: the size limit (a client can bypass any store)

keyPoints.text: Trimming, enum narrowing and the size hint stay on the client for fast feedback.
keyPoints.quote: trimming, enum narrowing and the size hint are still useful for fast feedback.

keyPoints.text: No client validator can establish identity, tenant access, or whether a photo is trustworthy.
keyPoints.quote: No client validator can establish identity, tenant access, or trustworthiness of a photo.

questions.prompt: Exercise 5 changes the RouteIQ delivery note limit to 50 characters. Describe a complete change: where the limit lives and how it is shared, which boundary cases to run, what the driver must see, how to check proofs, events and exports for consistency, and what happens to notes that were already persisted at the old limit (and how you prove it).

keyPoints.text: Change the single note-limit policy that both delivery proofs and failure notes use.
keyPoints.quote: Change the single note-limit policy used by both delivery proofs and failure notes

keyPoints.text: Run boundary cases at 49, 50 and 51 characters.
keyPoints.quote: run boundary cases at 49, 50 and 51 characters.

keyPoints.text: Make the limit visible in the driver form guidance so a person knows it before submitting (today neither note input shows one).
keyPoints.quote: Review the driver form guidance so a person knows the limit before submitting.

keyPoints.text: The stored proof and the event must hold the same retained note.
keyPoints.quote: Verify that both the stored proof and the event contain the same retained note

keyPoints.text: Check CSV and JSON exports rather than adding a second truncation rule in reporting.
keyPoints.quote: rather than silently applying a second truncation rule in reporting.

keyPoints.text: A shared exported constant keeps UI copy and validation in agreement; do not copy the number into multiple components.
keyPoints.quote: avoid copying the number into multiple components.

keyPoints.text: The change governs new writes only: existing 500-character notes are not rewritten during hydration, so keep them intact or add a separately tested migration, and document the choice.
keyPoints.quote: Existing persisted 500-character notes are not rewritten by the new-write sanitizer during hydration.

keyPoints.text: Prove the difference with one hydrated old note and one newly recorded 51-character note.
keyPoints.quote: Test one hydrated old note and one newly recorded 51-character note to demonstrate the difference.

questions.prompt: The senior review notes list three defects found by reading RouteIQ's code: recordDelivery and stop transitions, the failure toast, and how note length limits are counted. For each, say what the code does, why it matters, and (where the guide gives one) how the current UI gets away with it and whether any test covers it, or how to fix it.

keyPoints.text: recordDelivery returns early only for an unknown stop id; it never checks the stop's status.
keyPoints.quote: It returns early only when the stop id is unknown

keyPoints.text: So calling it on an already delivered or failed stop appends another delivered event.
keyPoints.quote: Calling it on a stop that is already `delivered` or `failed` appends another `delivered` event.

keyPoints.text: The UI only avoids this by closing the sheet first; the hardened store boundary does not enforce the transition, and no test covers it.
keyPoints.quote: the store boundary that this course hardens does not enforce the transition. No test covers it.

keyPoints.text: markFailed shows "Marked failed" unconditionally, ignoring recordFailure's result, while confirmDelivery checks result.ok.
keyPoints.quote: shows "Marked failed" unconditionally

keyPoints.text: If the reason guard rejects, the driver is told the opposite of what happened.
keyPoints.quote: If the reason guard ever rejects, the driver is told the opposite of what happened.

keyPoints.text: Length limits count UTF-16 code units: cleanText's slice can cut an emoji in half and persist a lone surrogate.
keyPoints.quote: which counts UTF-16 code units, so the emoji is cut in half and a lone surrogate is persisted.

keyPoints.text: Slicing Array.from(value) cuts by code point instead.
keyPoints.quote: `Array.from(value).slice(0, max).join('')` cuts by code point instead.
